title: Split a port's maintenance budget and read the answer

blocks.text: A port authority splits its maintenance budget across its terminals. Each terminal returns a value per $k spent, its work needs dock-crew hours per $k, it has a number of crew hours available, and some terminals have a floor the harbor board requires them to get. The authority wants the best split and, just as much, an answer it can read: did the solve succeed, what does each terminal get, and which limits decided it.
With $`T`$ the terminals, $`v_t`$ the value per $k, $`h_t`$ the crew hours per $k, $`H_t`$ the hours available, $`f_t`$ the floor and $`B`$ the budget:

\begin{aligned}
\max \;& \sum_{t \in T} v_t\, x_t \\
\text{s.t. }& \sum_{t \in T} x_t \le B && && \text{(budget)} \\
& h_t\, x_t \le H_t && \forall t \in T && \text{(labour}_t) \\
& x_t \ge f_t && \forall t \in T,\ f_t > 0 && \text{(floor}_t) \\
& x_t \ge 0 && \forall t \in T
\end{aligned}

$`x_t`$ is continuous, in $k. Write `split(terminals, budget)` in `split.py`. It builds this model with the row names shown (`budget`, `labour_north`, `floor_east`, ...; a terminal with floor 0 gets no floor row), solves it with GLOP and returns `(status, value, amounts, full)`:

items: `status`: the name of the termination reason, such as `"OPTIMAL"` or `"INFEASIBLE"`;

when the status is `OPTIMAL`: `value`, the objective value; `amounts`, a dict from terminal name to its amount, not rounded; and `full`, the set of names of the rows whose activity is within `TOL` ($`10^{-6}`$) of their lower or their upper bound;
otherwise `None, None, None`, because a solve that found no split has nothing to report.

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

TOL = 1e-6


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Terminal:
    name: str
    value: float          # value returned per $k spent
    hours_per_k: float    # dock-crew hours per $k of work
    hours: float          # dock-crew hours available
    floor: float = 0      # least it must get, $k (0: no floor)


def split(terminals: list[Terminal], budget: float):
    """Solve the split LP with GLOP. Returns (status, value, amounts, full rows)."""
    # TODO: the model of the statement (variables, rows, objective), a GLOP solve, the status first,
    # then the value, the amounts and the names of the full rows.
    return "NOT_SOLVED", None, None, None

if __name__ == "__main__":
    port = [Terminal("north", 1.2, 2, 400), Terminal("south", 0.9, 1, 300), Terminal("east", 0.7, 4, 800)]
    print(split(port, 600))

cases.says: an allowed budget returns OPTIMAL, the best value, the amounts and the full rows
amounts are continuous, so a budget of 600.5 is split to the fraction
floors that no split can meet give INFEASIBLE with no value, amounts or rows
a floor is a least amount, so a terminal worth less still gets its floor
a row is full when its activity sits on either bound, the lower one included
no amount is negative, even when moving money from a poor terminal would pay

origin.section: GLOP Solves It: Read the Status, Then the Amounts, Then the Rows

concepts: an amount of money is a continuous variable whose lower bound must be stated
a solve is read status first, then amounts, then each row's activity against its bound
